title: A clause a decide line adds is covered by proof coverage
intention: A falsifier clause that a decide line adds is a clause proof coverage demands a tooth for, exactly as it demands one for a clause written in the falsifier field.
why: Peer F17(a) (2026-10-07): proof_coverage.clauses() reads only the falsifier field, so clause (4) of 11cd253f10bc, entered through decide line D6 ('A falsifier clause (4) is added by this line'), was invisible to lacks(). F17 ruled the falsifier is not edited to fit the gate, so 11cd's hollow had to red tooth 4 by hand, and its measured_at_build (5) records that: 'recorded by hand because proof_coverage reads only the falsifier's clauses 1-3 (F17a)'. A clause the gate cannot see is a clause that can enter PROVED with no tooth (Law 8).
traces_to: Law 8 (nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass: a clause with no demanded tooth enters PROVED unproven) and Law 4 (11cd's clause (4) was covered only because the builder reddened its tooth by hand — policy where physics should be).
how: cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py: clauses(ticket) keeps its falsifier reading unchanged and appends, in decision order and without duplicates, every clause key a decision's text declares added in the form 'falsifier clause (N) is added by this line' (the phrasing of the one such line in the corpus, 11cd253f10bc D6). lacks() then names a missing PROVES key for such a clause with no other change. One new proof in cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proofs/.

proves_red.1: falsifier '(1) a (2) b (3) c' plus a decision 'A falsifier clause (4) is added by this line: d' gives clauses() == ['1','2','3','4'];
proves_red.2: lacks() over that ticket, against a fixture proof whose PROVES declares '1'-'3' only, returns a lack naming clause '4';
proves_red.3: a decision text 'D2 (6) stands; tooth (4) is green' adds nothing (clauses() == ['1','2','3']).

falsifier.horizon: Hollow: revert cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py, teeth 1-2 red, tooth 3 green either way. Horizon: the next decide line that adds a clause is covered by lacks() with no hand-reddened tooth.

watchme: none, because its live reading is the clearance gate itself: every PROVED crossing calls /home/akien/dev/src/cairn/cairn/tools/proof_coverage/proof_coverage.py lacks(), and an added clause without a tooth refuses there
